findings.reason: the done-when demands the one-pass result ("one opening template and one flux-surface-average equation" after an apply), which the evidence says refinement without deterministic insertion cannot produce, so a node could complete every listed repair and still re-plan calls instead of converging.
findings.text: §3's repairs 2 and 4 enforce the opening and the equation by refusal/refine at acceptance only; the citation they rest on, `shc-convergence-diagnosis.html` ("Smallest deterministic route to one converged apply"), pairs validation with insertion — "Instantiate the selected density template with the member's subject and place the canonical flux-surface-average equation in one fixed form" — and states plainly that "A refusal alone prevents a false acceptance but cannot guarantee a one-pass result; deterministic insertion plus validation supplies it"

findings.reason: three of the four repairs are the whole point of the redesign and each is invisible to the stated measure, so the node cannot show its new guards fire — the same defect the earlier review raised against §4's done-when and which §3 now reproduces with new guards.
findings.text: the done-when's controls cover the anchor-first ordering (a deliberately failed anchor), the recommended-name guard (the refusal test fails when the guard is removed) and the snapshot, but nothing makes the new enforcement happen: no test shows a non-conforming opening is refused/refined (repair 2), a member with a divergent equation is refused (repair 4), a cross-family target is no longer counted dead (repair 2/1), or a continuation reuses a recorded anchor (repair 3), so a uniform after-column of "one opening / one equation / zero dead links" passes whether those guards fire or are absent

findings.reason: a single review verdict cannot close an apply mechanism plus four enforcement changes across three modules, and repair 1 belongs to §2's report surface, so leaving it under §3's goal mixes the section that a review can close with one it cannot.
findings.text: §3's one goal ("Apply: the anchor first, the members from the anchor") now carries four independent repairs whose write surfaces diverge: repair 1 changes the §2 report's link scoping in `review/audits.py:405` (a report-only fix the diagnosis even says "cannot repair this scoped-report counting defect" from the write side), repair 2 changes the documentation acceptance path in `workers.py`, repair 3 persists the anchor in the plan/run path, repair 4 adds an equation-equality gate

findings.reason: all four repairs land regardless and their order is a sequencing preference, not a redirect, so only the sentence's claim about the citation is wrong.
findings.text: §3 says the repairs follow "in the order the evidence ranks them", but the cited ranking orders opening+equation enforcement first and graph-wide link resolution second, while the plan places link resolution first and splits the evidence's single top-ranked item (opening and equation together) into repairs 2 and 4

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `protection.py`, `harmonize.py`, `workers.py`, `audits.py`, `families.py` and `standard_names/manifests/reviews/` all resolve, and the cited `shc-convergence-diagnosis.html` href (extensionless, resolved as `.html`) exists.

rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §3's gate evidence sits in the plan's evidence tree (`docs/evidence/fragments/sn-harmonize-command/`), not in a session scratchpad or node-local temporary path.

rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §3's single done-when now closes over the apply mechanism, the recommended-name guard and four independent enforcement repairs in `audits.py`, `workers.py`, `families.py` and `harmonize.py`, so no one verdict can close the node.
